To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) pentose sugars are metabolized through the pentose phosphate pathway and are selectively channelled to ribonucleotidic precursors and (ii) hemicellulosics are metabolized through a glycolytic pathway and are selectively channeled towards biofuel precussors.

(1) C. acetobutylcum preferentially channels pentose sugars towards ribonucleotid synthesis; (2) C. acetbutylcum preferentially channel hexose sugars through glycolysis towards biofuel precussor synthesis; and (3) the metabolic hierarchy of C. acetbutylicum is substrate‐dependent.
C. acetobutylcium preferentially invests hemicellulosics into pentose‐based nucleotide biosynthesis and glucose into the biofuel precursers.

the understanding of the metabolic hierarchy of sugars in the context of biofuel precursor production in C. acetbutylicum, which is important in the context of mixed‐sugar fermentation.

the metabolic hierarchies that govern the utilization of the different sugars in the hemicellulolytic hydrolysate and the impact this has on biofuel precursor production.

The main takeaway from our work is that
C. acetobutylcium can selectively route the hemicelluloses towards biofuel precursers, which is important for biofuel production.
C. acetobutiicum can be engineered to preferentially utilize the hemicelluloses over cellulose, and the pentose sugars can be diverted towards ribonucleotidic building blocks for RNA biosynthesis.
